registry.note: Dietary supplements are regulated as food, so recalls appear in FDA's food enforcement reports. No match means no recall is on file under this exact firm name — not that the company has a clean history.

data.summary: Thorne is an American health and wellness company that manufactures dietary supplements and health tests. It focuses on science-backed formulas and sells directly to consumers, health practitioners, and professional sports teams.
reputation_notes: Partnered with multiple United States national sports governing bodies.
Went public on the NASDAQ stock exchange in 2021.
Acquired by L Catterton and taken private in 2023.

business_model.basis: Sells products directly through its website, authorized online retailers, and medical practitioner channels without distributor recruitment.

caveats: Public batch-level certificates of analysis availability was not confirmed.

funding_independence.basis: A significant portion of clinical research on creatine monohydrate is sponsored or supported by commercial ingredient manufacturers and distributors.

publication_bias.basis: Meta-analyses have noted potential publication bias due to a high volume of small, positive performance trials and relatively few published negative trials.
signals: Asymmetry in funnel plots for small athletic performance trials
Over-representation of small positive studies in literature

caveats: Many trials receive independent university support alongside industry grants
Extensive long-term independent safety data exists alongside commercial trials

data.summary: Creatine monohydrate is a widely researched dietary supplement used primarily to increase muscle strength, power output, and lean body mass. Hundreds of human clinical trials support its effectiveness for high-intensity exercise performance. It is one of the most thoroughly studied athletic performance supplements available.

evidence_landscape.note: Extensive literature includes dozens of systematic reviews and meta-analyses covering performance, body composition, and therapeutic uses.

outcomes.population: Healthy adults and athletes undergoing resistance training
outcomes.note: Supported by numerous meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials showing consistent gains in maximal strength.
outcomes.dose_reading: 4.4 g/day sits inside the range the model recalls as effective (3 g–5 g).

outcomes.note: Consistently demonstrates modest increases in lean body mass compared to placebo when combined with training.
outcomes.dose_reading: 4.4 g/day sits inside the range the model recalls as effective (3 g–5 g).

outcomes.population: Stressed adults, vegetarians, and older adults
outcomes.note: Meta-analyses show potential benefits for memory and tasks during sleep deprivation, though findings in healthy unstressed adults are mixed.
outcomes.dose_reading: 4.4 g/day sits inside the range the model recalls as effective (3 g–5 g).

form_assessment.note: Creatine monohydrate has nearly 100% oral bioavailability (the amount that reaches the bloodstream) and remains the gold standard form in research.

safety_notes: Mild gastrointestinal distress or cramping can occur if taken with insufficient water.
Causes transient water retention, leading to minor weight gain.
Safe for long-term use in healthy individuals at standard daily doses of 3 to 5 grams.
caveats: Exact pooled effect sizes vary depending on the specific meta-analysis and subgroup analyzed.
Non-responders exist, as individuals with high baseline muscle creatine stores experience smaller benefits.

evidence_prior.disclaimer: This section is the model's own recollection of the literature — not trials we read, checked and can quote. Treat it as orientation. It carries no grade, because a grade means 'computed from extracted trials', and the two must not look alike.

census.means: How many trials EXIST. Not what they found — direction and quality require extraction, which has not been run for this product.
